properties.description:
The drift class it exists for: a bump lands in a manifest and the prose still advertises the previous value, so a reader orienting from AGENTS.md gets a confident wrong answer — and confidently wrong is worse than absent, because nobody goes to check.

ITS ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE FROM THE UPSTREAM SCRIPT IT WAS ADAPTED FROM is the thing worth knowing about it: a pattern that matches nothing FAILS rather than passing quietly. The upstream greps with `|| true` and its own header admits that rewording a doc line disables the corresponding check silently. reflow2 holds req:no-silent-fallback at critical priority, so here rewording breaks the build loudly and both sides get fixed together.

EXTENDED 2026-09-07 FROM 3 CLAIMS TO 11. It guarded version strings only. Retiring QualityGate moved the node count 29 to 28, and a sweep found the EDGE count in the same four sentences had been wrong for weeks — three said 60 and one said 64 against a real 65 — because nothing checked structural claims at all. It now reads both counts from schema/*.yaml and asserts them across AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/overview.md and docs/interaction-surfaces.md.

Each schema-count pattern matches EVERY occurrence in its file rather than the first, which is the specific lesson from that drift: README carried the size in two sentences and both were wrong, so a check anchored on one would have passed while the other rotted.

REGISTERED LATE, on the day it was extended. It had been a CI gate outside the design record, which is the same silence that let constructors_preserve.rs guard a class while its own scope was wrong.
properties.name: check_doc_versions.py — the gate that asserts a doc's factual claims against what the build actually says, where a pattern matching nothing is a FAILURE
